 Canadiens tap Oliver Kapanen to play larger role after ‘huge loss’ of Nick Suzuki 
 "Nobody can really fill (his) shoes," Cole Caufield says of Habs captain's injury. "We know that as a group." 
 By 
 Herb Zurkowsky 
 October 22, 2026 at 3:01 p.m. 
 So, now what?
 The loss of captain Nick Suzuki for two to four weeks is only one part of the story enveloping the Canadiens, who are off to an inconsistent start this season as they prepare for the beginning of a four-game road trip Friday at Chicago (8 p.m., TSN2, RDS, TSN Radio-690, 98.5 FM). 
 Suzuki blocked a shot with his left hand Tuesday against San Jose and received treatment after the game.
 If a team assumes the identity of its captain, the Canadiens have never had to deal with life without him — Suzuki has played 546 consecutive games since making his NHL debut with Montreal on Oct. 3, 2019.
 Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki, who will miss two to four weeks after blocking a shot with his left hand Tuesday against the San Jose Sharks, has played 546 consecutive games since making his NHL debut with Montreal on Oct. 3, 2019. John Mahoney / Montreal Gazette 
 That also means Martin St. Louis, who arrived behind the bench on Feb. 10, 2022, has never had to coach a game without his captain, inspirational leader and conduit between management and the players.
 It could be a daunting task for the team (4-3-2) which already is having difficulty holding leads in the third period.
 “We just fall back on the collective game,” St. Louis said after Thursday’s practice in Brossard. “I think that’s how we’ve done it. To me, it’s the next man up. I don’t know what the challenges are going to be, but I’ll see. I feel I’ll be ready for whatever. Obviously, I had to be ready for today. He’s not going to play, so you’ve got to plan, get organized. And that’s what we did.
 “We’re just going to keep going,” he added. “It’s a big piece, but we’ll be ready for whatever comes. We’re always going to fall back on our collective game.”
 With a goal and assist against the Sharks, Suzuki increased his season totals to five goals and 12 points. He leads the Canadiens in points and is one goal behind Cole Caufield , the left-winger on the team’s top line, which also includes Juraj Slafkovsky.
 Oliver Kapanen will replace Suzuki on the line and on the No. 1 power-play unit. But since management failed to land a second-line centre during the summer — one of the team’s biggest off-season needs — it will attempt to remain competitive in the tough Atlantic Division without its first-line centre.
 The Canadiens are already missing talented Russian forward Ivan Demidov , who blocked a shot during an exhibition game and continues to use a walking boot. Demidov had a goal and assist in two games after producing 19 goals and 62 assists last season as a rookie.
 He didn’t accompany the team on its flight to Chicago. The trip continues Sunday night, with the outdoor Heritage Classic in Winnipeg, followed by stops in St. Louis on Tuesday and Dallas on Thursday. 
 The Canadiens also recalled forward Owen Beck on Thursday after he scored an empty-net goal Wednesday for the Laval Rocket in a 5-1 win over Syracuse.
 “It’s a huge loss,” Caufield said. “Any time you lose a guy like (Suzuki) it’s obviously tough for the group. But collectively, we’ve all got to step up and try to fill that (void) a little bit. We’ve just got to do the job in front of us. It’s not going to be easy, but (Slafkovsky) and I can step up and try to do more for the team. I think everyone as a whole can step up and take this time to improve their game.

 Why do blunder-prone Canadiens continue to play high-risk hockey? 
 “He’s a guy that has never missed a game,” Caufield added. “It obviously sucks. It’s tough news. It’s something new to him, too. He’ll work his ass off to get back as soon as possible. We’ll try to step up our game for him. It’s a huge loss. Nobody can really fill (Suzuki’s) shoes. We know that as a group.”
 While the pressure might intensify for Caufield — who scored a team-leading 51 goals last season — to continue producing at an even greater pace, he said those expectations haven’t changed.
 Caufield said Kapanen is a smart player who can be inserted anywhere in the lineup. Kapanen, who overcame his own early-season lower-body injury, missed the first seven games. Since returning two games ago , he played right wing on the fourth line with centre Jake Evans and Kirby Dach. Kapanen is seeking his first point after scoring 22 goals and adding 15 assists last season.
 “It might look like it’s a little challenge for us, but it’s part of hockey and part of the season,” said Slafkovsky, who escaped relatively unscathed after taking a puck to the face during Thursday’s practice. “We’re going to have guys that go down, but you have to play like they’re there. Obviously, we’re going to miss (Suzuki) but you’ve just got to play hard. The important thing is to win games. Nothing changes for us.”
